body: Godot `v4.4.1.stable.fedora.49a5bc7b6` works for me. I would verify that vulkan is actually installed and working (The overridden state can happen if vulkan is not installed). You can do `dnf install mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-loader vulkaninfo`. Then see the output of `vulkaninfo`.
The Radeon R9 390 does not have full Vulkan support due to missing hardware features (its Direct3D 12 support is also limited for similar reasons). Even if it worked, it would likely be quite slow.

That runs forward+ without issue with my GPU. Also, initially the rpm install also ran fine with no issues. This only changed within the past day or so.

Flatpaks come with their own versions of the Mesa drivers.

So you likely have functional drivers installed via Flatpak / Discover to flatpak apps, but you don't have the proper vulkan drivers RPM installed for native packages.

Try to install `mesa-vulkan-drivers`.

@akien-mga When I run install that package I  receive the following output:
Package "mesa-vulkan-drivers-25.0.6-1.fc42.i686" is already installed.

Nothing to do.

However than running vulkaninfo provides the following output:
ERROR: [Loader Message] Code 0 : vkCreateInstance: Found no drivers!
Cannot create Vulkan instance.
This problem is often caused by a faulty installation of the Vulkan driver or attempting to use a GPU that does not support Vulkan.
ERROR at /builddir/build/BUILD/vulkan-tools-1.4.313.0-build/Vulkan-Tools-vulkan-sdk-1.4.313.0/vulkaninfo/./vulkaninfo.h:573:vkCreateInstance failed with ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE_DRIVER

> [@akien-mga](https://github.com/akien-mga) When I run install that package I receive the following output:
> Package "mesa-vulkan-drivers-25.0.6-1.fc42.i686" is already installed.

That's the 32-bit version. Assuming you're on an x86_64 system, you're missing the x86_64 version of the package.

Try this:
```
sudo dnf install --forcearch=x86_64 mesa-vulkan-drivers
```

If that doesn't work, it might be that you disabled/deleted your x86_64 DNF sources.

BTW I'm on Fedora 42 too and I had mesa-vulkan-drivers-25.0.4-2.fc42. I see there's an update to 25.0.6-1.fc42 which was pushed ~today~ [2 days ago](https://bodhi.fedoraproject.org/updates/FEDORA-2025-cfc1f6c296).

You were likely unlucky and did the upgrade when not all packages were synced on your mirror and you ended up in a broken state with only partially installed upgrade, which removed the old version without having a new counterpart available to install. DNF should have warned about this but not sure if Discover would do too.

I'm sure this is a local issue due to a failed update, so closing the issue as it's not a Godot bug. But feel free to ask if you're still stuck fixing your packages.

I was able to resolve my issue with the assistance of AI eventually running these two commands completely cleaned up my vulkaninfo errors:

```
sudo dnf remove mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-validation-layers
sudo dnf install mesa-vulkan-drivers vulkan-validation-layers
```

hopefully this saves someone else time in the future.
@Calinou @akien-mga may want to relabel this as resolved with this comment as the solution so that if people run into this issue in the future they can try this out.
